top3.why: PhilaMOCA's monthly Psychotronic Film Society meetup is dedicated to the deliberately weird end of genre cinema — exploitation, horror ephemera, and whatever else doesn't fit a normal repertory slot. This screening also closes voting for the 2026 Psychotronic Awards, so it's a bigger night than the usual meetup. Doors 7:00 PM, screening 7:30; Callowhill, a couple of blocks from the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop.

Soup Can Magazine's roving art-and-poetry pop-up lands at Tattooed Mom with a lineup of Philly writers (Shannon Frost Greenstein among them) — free, no cover, no RSVP required. Tattooed Mom's live-music and performance shows are on hold under an ongoing city permit dispute, but non-musical nights like this one are explicitly still running, so it's a real option, not a maybe.

DOMi & JD Beck are jazz-fusion prodigies barely into their twenties, touring behind the follow-up to their Blue Note debut — a genre-scrambling, virtuosic set that name-checks Herbie Hancock as readily as hyperpop. All ages, standing-room general admission. Fishtown/Olde Richmond, about a 15-minute walk from the Market-Frankford Line's Girard stop, or the 15 trolley to Frankford & Delaware right across the street.

top3.why: Militarie Gun channel hardcore's speed and DIY ethic through unpolished, almost pop hooks and Ian Shelton's wry, anti-scene-politics lyrics — a genuinely vital band in a genre that's mostly nostalgia acts right now. 21+, $20. Doors 6:00 PM, show 7:00; Callowhill, about two blocks from the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop.

Howard Zinn's one-man play imagines Karl Marx bargaining his way back from the afterlife to defend himself against 2026 America, delivered by longtime interpreter Bob Weick, who's performed the role hundreds of times worldwide. Sharp, funny, and unapologetically didactic — “the words the billionaire class doesn't want you to hear.” $20; opens tonight and runs most of the week. (No confirmed street address for Broken Mirror Studio — sources disagree between a Broad Street and a North 9th Street location, so confirm before heading out.)

A former Cirque du Soleil performer's autobiographical solo show tracing a childhood inside a brutal military-style circus training system, from age four to a premiere at nine — framed as reclaiming a body and voice that discipline tried to own. Opens tonight, running three nights. $25; Olde Kensington, about a 10-minute walk from the Market-Frankford Line's Girard stop.

top3.why: Minyo Crusaders reinvent Japanese min'yō (traditional folk song) as cumbia, ska, and tropical dance music — bandleader Katsumi Tanaka started the project after the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami sent him digging into folk songs he'd ignored his whole life. Their first-ever North American tour, with Mariposas Galácticas opening. Callowhill, a couple of blocks from the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop.

Poet Hillary Gonzalez reads from their new collection “Where the Osprey Nest” (Palewell Press) — meditations on ospreys, herons, grief, and the idea that we're not separate from nature but part of it — followed by a Q&A and a briefing on the campaign to save the declining East Coast osprey population. Classic Wooden Shoe programming: politically engaged literature with a concrete cause attached.

Secret Cinema's rare-16mm-print series turns its projector on mid-century design films for this one — “Form and Function at Mid-Century,” part of an ongoing archive-diving project distinct from the Rotunda's standing Wednesday jam session happening down the hall. Free/PWYW, University City.

top3.why: Fabio Frizzi — the composer behind Lucio Fulci's gore classics *Zombi 2*, *The Beyond*, and *City of the Living Dead* — performs those scores live on his first North American tour in support of them. This is about as direct a hit on PhilaMOCA's whole reason for existing as a booking gets: Italian horror, live, at the venue built for exactly this. Doors 7:30 PM, show 8:00; Callowhill, a couple of blocks from the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop.

A workshop on mutual aid as organizing practice, not just charity — how to build durable, non-hierarchical support networks rather than one-off relief drives. Wooden Shoe's entire program runs on this kind of practical political education, free or pay-what-you-can as always.

A full, start-to-finish listening session for Stevie Wonder's *Songs in the Key of Life* — the kind of deep-catalog, no-distractions format that lets a classic actually land instead of playing in the background. Fits the same archival/repertory lane as the city's better jazz nights, just for soul. Fishtown/Olde Kensington, about a 10-minute walk from the Market-Frankford Line's Berks stop.

top3.why: Three-quarters of the original Sex Pistols — Steve Jones, Paul Cook, and Glen Matlock — touring with Frank Carter (Gallows/Rattlesnakes) on vocals for the 50th anniversary of the band that arguably started UK punk. This date was postponed from last fall after Jones broke his wrist; he's recovered and the tour is back on. All ages. Fishtown, about a 10-minute walk from the Market-Frankford Line's Girard stop.

Iffy Books turns 5 — a genuine institution-in-the-making for DIY electronics, speculative fiction, and leftist politics in this city — with a dance party at Vox Populi's Black Box space (down the hall from Iffy's original location), DJ sets from Nila Paradise and Ishtar Sr. among others. A rare chance to celebrate the place itself rather than just its programming.

Ray Cappo — frontman of straight-edge hardcore pioneers Youth of Today and, later, Krishnacore band Shelter — talks about the 90s Krishnacore movement, the scene where hardcore's discipline and Hare Krishna devotion collided. He spent six years as a celibate monk before returning to music; expect a genuinely unusual insider account, not a nostalgia set. South Street, easy walk from Center City.

top3.why: Iron Lung — one of grindcore's defining acts, a duo that's been redefining how much noise two people can make since the 90s — headline a five-band bill with Hologram, Pray To Be Saved, Early Grave, and Malform. An R5 all-ages show at the city's most storied punk venue; earplugs strongly advised.

A prisoner-solidarity event in Wooden Shoe's downstairs space — likely tied to Books Through Bars, the Philly-based prison-literacy project, though the listing itself is thin on specifics, so treat details as worth confirming at the door. Free/PWYW, as nearly everything at Wooden Shoe is.

Indy Hall turns 20 — one of the oldest independent coworking spaces in the country, founded in Old City in 2006, before “coworking” was even a common word. The party frames it as two decades of showing up for each other rather than just surviving, which tracks with the community's whole ethos: “take care of yourself, take care of each other, take care of this place.” Northern Liberties, near 2nd & Spring Garden, a few blocks from the Market-Frankford Line.

top3.why: Buzzcocks — one of the foundational UK punk bands, the ones who basically invented the punk love song — play a WXPN-presented show at Underground Arts. Still touring on the strength of a back catalog that shaped everything from pop-punk to indie rock. 21+, doors 7:00 PM, show 8:00. Callowhill, a couple of blocks from the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop.

Satirical immersive theater staged as a mandatory corporate motivational seminar — fictional “Ramco Laboratories” brings in Luigi Mangione (framed here as a corporate-America folk antihero, not the real defendant in an active criminal case) to inspire employees to “take your shot.” Pointed, uncomfortable, and exactly the kind of anti-corporate satire that doesn't get made by anyone with something to lose. Chinatown North/Callowhill, close to the Broad Street Line's Race-Vine or Spring Garden stops.

Two castaways attempt to hunt and eat a pig with predictably dire results — a genre-blending piece built on heavy movement, mask, and sound work that uses survival-horror absurdity to get at something more serious about trauma and complicity. Fringe programming at First Unitarian Church, better known for its punk shows.
